correctness.rationale: The minimal automaton has state residues and delta(r,d)=br+d mod m, every state accessible and separately observed. A repeated state with distinct incoming digits at positions i<j yields positive prefix-value difference multiple of m but not b, bounded by b^L-b; thus m<=b^L-b. Conversely with K=b^(L-1)-1 and m<=bK one may write m=cK+t for c in {0,...,b-1}, t in [0,K]; the word with first digit c and length-(L-1) tail for t repeats residue at its last prefix but changes incoming digit because b does not divide m. If b divides m no distinct digit collision exists. Allouche--Yao published shortest-inhomogeneous-path theorem then gives opacity, and interval counting of nonmultiples b yields (b-1)^2 b^(L-2), including L=2 and m=1. The witness proves the unbounded statement, not bounded checking alone.
